needs.role: Stationary, indestructible practice target providing the hitbox the player punches; user pre-approved this exact asset.
needs.constraints: Must resolve to assetId 1245720733 (creator Xtrah962). Inspect its embedded script (scriptCount:1) to confirm it does not deal damage, move, fight back, or knock itself down; must remain anchored/collidable and support a small nudge/flash reaction without falling over or being destroyed.

intent.experienceRole: This is the central object of the entire training loop: every punch, VFX burst, SFX cue and counter increment exists to register contact against this dummy, so its hitbox geometry and passive behavior directly gate whether the core loop functions.
intent.interaction: Non-attacking, non-moving prop: the player approaches and punches it; on a confirmed server-side hit it briefly flashes/nudges as feedback, then immediately returns to its resting stationary pose. It never damages the player or loses health itself.
reusableFeatures: Existing hitbox/collision geometry for hit-detection overlap
Any embedded idle/resting animation or physical joints usable for a brief nudge reaction
Embedded script behavior (scriptCount:1) that must be inspected for conflicting damage/AI logic before reuse

needs.role: Source of the R15 windup/strike/recovery punching animation clip played on the player's character when they throw a punch; user pre-approved this exact asset and clip.
needs.constraints: Must resolve to assetId 12061946559 (creator Auevi), embedded clip key 1/1/18/1. Inspect for R15 rig compatibility and for distinguishable windup, strike and recovery phases so the server can time the hit-detection check to the strike frame.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the visible, timed physical action of punching that the player's input maps to; without it the core loop has no observable attack animation and the strike-frame hit-detection timing has nothing to synchronize against.
intent.interaction: Plays fully on the player's character each time they press the punch input; the strike portion is the moment the server checks for a hit against the dummy. Animation completion (recovery) also gates the punch cooldown before another swing can be thrown.

userSources.text: want a fighting game with punching animation, vfx, sfx, target dummy, hit counter for everytime you hit the dummy

Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.

A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.

A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.

playerExperience.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
playerExperience.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.

Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.

A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.

requirements.description: When a player's character respawns, humanoid/animator/root-part references used by punch validation and animation playback are rebound, and the HUD persists correctly without duplicating or losing the session's hit count.

requirements.description: Multiple players can each punch the shared dummy independently; one player's hits, cooldown, or reset action never affect another player's counter or cooldown state.

userSources.text: want a fighting game with punching animation, vfx, sfx, target dummy, hit counter for everytime you hit the dummy

Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.

A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.

A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.

playerExperience.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
playerExperience.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.
requirements.acceptance: The combined VFX color/timing and SFX character read as a clean, satisfying 'thwack' consistent with a training-room tone rather than gritty combat, verified by inspecting the imported VFX/SFX assets.

requirements.description: A third-person camera follows the player, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during punching, using the default direct-control scheme.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.
requirements.acceptance: During normal play near the dummy, the default third-person camera keeps both the player character and the dummy visible on screen.

requirements.description: The server independently validates every punch attempt (range to dummy, cooldown state, character alive) and performs the authoritative hit-detection check; client input and reported hits are never trusted directly.
requirements.acceptance: A modified or spoofed client punch/hit request that violates range, cooldown or animation-lock rules is rejected server-side and does not increment the counter.

requirements.description: Each player's hit count and punch cooldown state are stored server-side, keyed by player/UserId, updated on confirmed hits, zeroed on reset requests, and cleaned up when the player leaves.
requirements.acceptance: Server-side state exists per connected player, updates only in response to that player's confirmed hits/reset requests, and is removed without error when the player leaves the game.

requirements.description: When a player's character respawns, humanoid/animator/root-part references used by punch validation and animation playback are rebound, and the HUD persists correctly without duplicating or losing the session's hit count.
requirements.acceptance: After a manual respawn, the player can still punch and register hits, the HUD shows the same session hit count as before respawn, and no duplicate HUD or stale connections are created.

requirements.description: Multiple players can each punch the shared dummy independently; one player's hits, cooldown, or reset action never affect another player's counter or cooldown state.
requirements.acceptance: With two or more players punching the same dummy, each player's own Hit Counter and cooldown update independently and a reset by one player does not change another player's counter.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: The user has already approved four specific Marketplace assets covering the bulk of requested behavior and media: (1) a Training Dummy model as the stationary practice target, (2) an R15 Punching Animations pack with a specific embedded clip for the windup/strike/recovery punch, (3) a Punch Impact SFX cue, and (4) a Hit VFX (boxing impact) model. Each must go through discovery/import/verification (Takko) before integration: inspect the dummy's existing script (scriptCount:1) to confirm it doesn't fight back, damage the player, or move on its own before reuse; inspect the animation model's embedded clip (key 1/1/18/1) for R15 compatibility and windup/strike/recovery timing; verify the SFX loads and plays through the audio pipeline; inspect the VFX model's particle/attachment rig for one-shot burst emission suitable for warm-accent impact feedback. Only the missing integration is authored: server-authoritative punch validation (cooldown, distance, hit window) and per-player hit-count state, since none of the four assets provide multiplayer-safe server logic; a reaction/feedback service that triggers the verified VFX/SFX/dummy nudge on a confirmed hit; and a HUD that displays/reset the counter with a pop animation, since no asset supplies UI. If inspection of the dummy's embedded script reveals damage/knockdown/AI behavior that conflicts with the 'stationary, indestructible' requirement, or if the animation clip is not R15-compatible or lacks distinct windup/strike/recovery phases, or if the SFX/VFX fail pipeline verification, these are reported as blocked gaps rather than silently replaced with procedural substitutes.

playerExperience.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
playerExperience.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

requirements.description: Player controls a single fighter who can move around and throw a punch at a stationary training dummy; approaching, punching and landing hits forms the entire playable loop.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.
requirements.acceptance: From spawn, the player can walk toward the dummy and trigger a punch that can land on it, with no win/lose condition or opponent AI required.

Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.
requirements.acceptance: Repeated hits over any duration never reduce a health value, destroy the dummy, or cause it to attack the player; the dummy remains anchored/in place throughout play.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.
requirements.acceptance: The combined VFX color/timing and SFX character read as a clean, satisfying 'thwack' consistent with a training-room tone rather than gritty combat, verified by inspecting the imported VFX/SFX assets.

requirements.description: A compact, single-room gym/dojo space with a flat floor, the dummy fixed at a central point, and the player spawning a few paces in front of it with open space to reposition; no additional rooms, hazards or obstacles.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.
requirements.acceptance: The workspace contains one enclosed/open training room with a walkable floor, a centrally fixed dummy, and a collidable spawn point a short distance in front of it, with no additional gameplay areas.

requirements.description: The server independently validates every punch attempt (range to dummy, cooldown state, character alive) and performs the authoritative hit-detection check; client input and reported hits are never trusted directly.
requirements.acceptance: A modified or spoofed client punch/hit request that violates range, cooldown or animation-lock rules is rejected server-side and does not increment the counter.

requirements.description: Each player's hit count and punch cooldown state are stored server-side, keyed by player/UserId, updated on confirmed hits, zeroed on reset requests, and cleaned up when the player leaves.
requirements.acceptance: Server-side state exists per connected player, updates only in response to that player's confirmed hits/reset requests, and is removed without error when the player leaves the game.

requirements.description: When a player's character respawns, humanoid/animator/root-part references used by punch validation and animation playback are rebound, and the HUD persists correctly without duplicating or losing the session's hit count.
requirements.acceptance: After a manual respawn, the player can still punch and register hits, the HUD shows the same session hit count as before respawn, and no duplicate HUD or stale connections are created.

requirements.description: Multiple players can each punch the shared dummy independently; one player's hits, cooldown, or reset action never affect another player's counter or cooldown state.
requirements.acceptance: With two or more players punching the same dummy, each player's own Hit Counter and cooldown update independently and a reset by one player does not change another player's counter.

requirements.description: The four user-approved Marketplace assets (Training Dummy model, R15 punching animation pack, punch impact SFX, punch impact VFX model) are discovered, imported, inspected and integrated, preserving their existing verified behavior/media rather than being replaced with procedural substitutes.
requirements.acceptance: Each of the four approved assets is present in the scene/asset pipeline in a form that passes inspection and native verification, and gameplay scripts reference these imported assets directly instead of placeholder geometry, animation or sound.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: The user has already approved four specific Marketplace assets covering the bulk of requested behavior and media: (1) a Training Dummy model as the stationary practice target, (2) an R15 Punching Animations pack with a specific embedded clip for the windup/strike/recovery punch, (3) a Punch Impact SFX cue, and (4) a Hit VFX (boxing impact) model. Each must go through discovery/import/verification (Takko) before integration: inspect the dummy's existing script (scriptCount:1) to confirm it doesn't fight back, damage the player, or move on its own before reuse; inspect the animation model's embedded clip (key 1/1/18/1) for R15 compatibility and windup/strike/recovery timing; verify the SFX loads and plays through the audio pipeline; inspect the VFX model's particle/attachment rig for one-shot burst emission suitable for warm-accent impact feedback. Only the missing integration is authored: server-authoritative punch validation (cooldown, distance, hit window) and per-player hit-count state, since none of the four assets provide multiplayer-safe server logic; a reaction/feedback service that triggers the verified VFX/SFX/dummy nudge on a confirmed hit; and a HUD that displays/reset the counter with a pop animation, since no asset supplies UI. If inspection of the dummy's embedded script reveals damage/knockdown/AI behavior that conflicts with the 'stationary, indestructible' requirement, or if the animation clip is not R15-compatible or lacks distinct windup/strike/recovery phases, or if the SFX/VFX fail pipeline verification, these are reported as blocked gaps rather than silently replaced with procedural substitutes.

referenceDecisions.reason: User approved the Training Dummy model (Xtrah962, assetId 1245720733) as the stationary practice target; its embedded script must be inspected to confirm it does not damage, knock down or fight back before reuse.
User approved the R15 Punching Animations pack (Auevi, assetId 12061946559, clipKey 1/1/18/1) as the source of the windup/strike/recovery punch animation instead of authoring a new animation.
User approved the Punch Impact 1 SFX (NickySergal, assetId 132504023010884) for the required impact sound cue; it must pass load/playback verification before use.
User approved the Hit VFX m1 boxing model (Spirit_Sage, assetId 86089736228455) for the impact burst; its particle/attachment rig must be inspected for one-shot burst emission before integration.

Mechanics proposal explicitly lists a combo streak indicator as an optional stretch mechanic; included as an optional-priority requirement and task so it can be skipped without blocking the core loop.
Mechanics proposal explicitly states no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy is in scope for this prototype.

userSources.text: want a fighting game with punching animation, vfx, sfx, target dummy, hit counter for everytime you hit the dummy

Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.

A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.

A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.

playerExperience.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
playerExperience.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.
requirements.acceptance: The combined VFX color/timing and SFX character read as a clean, satisfying 'thwack' consistent with a training-room tone rather than gritty combat, verified by inspecting the imported VFX/SFX assets.

requirements.description: A compact, single-room gym/dojo space with a flat floor, the dummy fixed at a central point, and the player spawning a few paces in front of it with open space to reposition; no additional rooms, hazards or obstacles.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.
requirements.acceptance: The workspace contains one enclosed/open training room with a walkable floor, a centrally fixed dummy, and a collidable spawn point a short distance in front of it, with no additional gameplay areas.

requirements.description: The server independently validates every punch attempt (range to dummy, cooldown state, character alive) and performs the authoritative hit-detection check; client input and reported hits are never trusted directly.
requirements.acceptance: A modified or spoofed client punch/hit request that violates range, cooldown or animation-lock rules is rejected server-side and does not increment the counter.

requirements.description: Each player's hit count and punch cooldown state are stored server-side, keyed by player/UserId, updated on confirmed hits, zeroed on reset requests, and cleaned up when the player leaves.
requirements.acceptance: Server-side state exists per connected player, updates only in response to that player's confirmed hits/reset requests, and is removed without error when the player leaves the game.

requirements.description: When a player's character respawns, humanoid/animator/root-part references used by punch validation and animation playback are rebound, and the HUD persists correctly without duplicating or losing the session's hit count.
requirements.acceptance: After a manual respawn, the player can still punch and register hits, the HUD shows the same session hit count as before respawn, and no duplicate HUD or stale connections are created.

requirements.description: Multiple players can each punch the shared dummy independently; one player's hits, cooldown, or reset action never affect another player's counter or cooldown state.
requirements.acceptance: With two or more players punching the same dummy, each player's own Hit Counter and cooldown update independently and a reset by one player does not change another player's counter.

requirements.description: The four user-approved Marketplace assets (Training Dummy model, R15 punching animation pack, punch impact SFX, punch impact VFX model) are discovered, imported, inspected and integrated, preserving their existing verified behavior/media rather than being replaced with procedural substitutes.
requirements.acceptance: Each of the four approved assets is present in the scene/asset pipeline in a form that passes inspection and native verification, and gameplay scripts reference these imported assets directly instead of placeholder geometry, animation or sound.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: The user has already approved four specific Marketplace assets covering the bulk of requested behavior and media: (1) a Training Dummy model as the stationary practice target, (2) an R15 Punching Animations pack with a specific embedded clip for the windup/strike/recovery punch, (3) a Punch Impact SFX cue, and (4) a Hit VFX (boxing impact) model. Each must go through discovery/import/verification (Takko) before integration: inspect the dummy's existing script (scriptCount:1) to confirm it doesn't fight back, damage the player, or move on its own before reuse; inspect the animation model's embedded clip (key 1/1/18/1) for R15 compatibility and windup/strike/recovery timing; verify the SFX loads and plays through the audio pipeline; inspect the VFX model's particle/attachment rig for one-shot burst emission suitable for warm-accent impact feedback. Only the missing integration is authored: server-authoritative punch validation (cooldown, distance, hit window) and per-player hit-count state, since none of the four assets provide multiplayer-safe server logic; a reaction/feedback service that triggers the verified VFX/SFX/dummy nudge on a confirmed hit; and a HUD that displays/reset the counter with a pop animation, since no asset supplies UI. If inspection of the dummy's embedded script reveals damage/knockdown/AI behavior that conflicts with the 'stationary, indestructible' requirement, or if the animation clip is not R15-compatible or lacks distinct windup/strike/recovery phases, or if the SFX/VFX fail pipeline verification, these are reported as blocked gaps rather than silently replaced with procedural substitutes.

referenceDecisions.reason: User approved the Training Dummy model (Xtrah962, assetId 1245720733) as the stationary practice target; its embedded script must be inspected to confirm it does not damage, knock down or fight back before reuse.
User approved the R15 Punching Animations pack (Auevi, assetId 12061946559, clipKey 1/1/18/1) as the source of the windup/strike/recovery punch animation instead of authoring a new animation.
User approved the Punch Impact 1 SFX (NickySergal, assetId 132504023010884) for the required impact sound cue; it must pass load/playback verification before use.
User approved the Hit VFX m1 boxing model (Spirit_Sage, assetId 86089736228455) for the impact burst; its particle/attachment rig must be inspected for one-shot burst emission before integration.

needs.role: Stationary, indestructible practice target providing the hitbox the player punches; user pre-approved this exact asset.

Inspect its embedded script (scriptCount:1) to confirm it does not deal damage, move, fight back, or knock itself down; must remain anchored/collidable and support a small nudge/flash reaction without falling over or being destroyed.

intent.experienceRole: This is the central object of the entire training loop: every punch, VFX burst, SFX cue and counter increment exists to register contact against this dummy, so its hitbox geometry and passive behavior directly gate whether the core loop functions.
intent.interaction: Non-attacking, non-moving prop: the player approaches and punches it; on a confirmed server-side hit it briefly flashes/nudges as feedback, then immediately returns to its resting stationary pose. It never damages the player or loses health itself.
reusableFeatures: Existing hitbox/collision geometry for hit-detection overlap
Any embedded idle/resting animation or physical joints usable for a brief nudge reaction
Embedded script behavior (scriptCount:1) that must be inspected for conflicting damage/AI logic before reuse

needs.role: Source of the R15 windup/strike/recovery punching animation clip played on the player's character when they throw a punch; user pre-approved this exact asset and clip.

userSources.text: want a fighting game with punching animation, vfx, sfx, target dummy, hit counter for everytime you hit the dummy

Core loop: the player controls a single fighter character who can move and throw a punch attack at a stationary training dummy. On input (e.g., left mouse click / controller face button / designated punch key), the character plays a punching animation (windup, strike, recovery). During the strike frame, a hit-detection check (e.g., a short-range capsule/sphere overlap or raycast in front of the character's fist) tests for contact with the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) trigger a punch-impact VFX (spark/burst) spawned at the contact point, (2) play a punch-impact SFX cue, (3) briefly flash or nudge the dummy (small physics impulse or scale/tint pulse) to sell the hit without destroying or knocking it over, (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1. The dummy is invulnerable/indestructible for this prototype — it does not take damage, lose health, or die; it exists purely as a hit-registration target. The Hit Counter is displayed on-screen (HUD) and updates in real time each time a hit registers; a reset button/key (e.g., R) zeroes the counter back to 0 for repeat practice sessions. Punch attacks have a short cooldown/animation-lock to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per single swing (one hit credited per successful strike animation). Basic movement (walk/strafe) lets the player reposition around the dummy to re-approach for the next punch. Optional stretch mechanic: a combo streak indicator that tracks consecutive hits within a time window, resetting the streak (but not the total counter) if the player misses or pauses too long.
Single-player prototype focused on one core loop: approach, punch, hit-register, counter increments — no win/lose condition or opponent AI beyond the passive dummy.
The target dummy is stationary, indestructible, and does not fight back or take damage; it is purely a hit-registration prop.
Only one punch attack type is required initially (a basic straight punch); additional attacks (kicks, combos, blocks) are out of scope unless requested.
Hit Counter persists only for the current play session and resets to 0 via a manual reset action (button/key), not automatically over time.
One VFX type (impact burst) and one SFX cue (punch impact) are sufficient for this first pass; no separate whiff/miss VFX or SFX unless requested later.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/overlap check timed to the punch animation's strike frame rather than full physics-based collision simulation.
Third-person camera perspective with direct character control (WASD/stick to move, one button to punch) is the assumed default control scheme.
No multiplayer, scoring leaderboard, or save/persistence of the hit counter across sessions is included in this scope.

A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.

A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
Single small enclosed or open training area is sufficient; no level progression, multiple rooms, or exploration space is needed.
HUD hit counter placement defaults to a standard top-of-screen position typical of counter/score displays.
Neutral, even lighting is assumed since no specific mood or time-of-day was requested.
No environmental hazards, destructible scenery, or secondary interactive objects are included beyond the player, dummy, and HUD.

playerExperience.title: Punch Trainer: Dummy Strike Arena
playerExperience.summary: A single-room martial-arts training prototype. From spawn, the player stands a few paces in front of a stationary training dummy in a compact, evenly lit gym/dojo space. A bold Hit Counter reads '0' near the top of the screen. The player walks/strafes into range (default WASD/stick movement) and presses the punch input (left click / face button / punch key); their character plays an R15 punching animation (windup → strike → recovery). If the strike frame lands within range of the dummy's hitbox, the server confirms the hit: a warm-accent impact VFX burst appears at the fist-dummy contact point, a sharp punch-impact SFX plays, the dummy flashes/nudges briefly without falling or taking damage, and the Hit Counter increments with a small scale-punch pop. A short cooldown prevents multiple credits per single swing, so the player naturally repositions and re-approaches for the next punch. Pressing R zeroes the counter for a fresh practice set. The dummy never fights back, never loses health, and cannot be destroyed — it exists purely to register and celebrate hits. This is a single-player-feeling core loop (approach → punch → hit-register → counter increments) built on Roblox's inherently multiplayer runtime, so hit counts, cooldowns and character bindings are tracked per player and cleaned up on respawn/leave. Four Marketplace assets were pre-approved by the user: the Training Dummy model, an R15 punching animation pack (specific embedded clip), a punch-impact SFX, and a punch-impact VFX model. These will be discovered, imported and inspected through the asset pipeline; only the missing server-authoritative validation, per-player state, HUD wiring and reaction glue will be authored. No win/lose condition, opponent AI, multiplayer competition, or counter persistence across sessions is in scope. Third-person default Roblox camera is assumed sufficient to frame both player and dummy. No unresolved consequential questions remain; defaults above are stated assumptions, not open items.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Clean, arcade-y dojo aesthetic: a compact, evenly lit single room (neutral flat lighting, no dramatic shadows) with the training dummy fixed at a central focal point and open floor space around it for repositioning. Materials stay simple and legible — light wood/mat flooring, plain walls — so the punch action and impact feedback read clearly against a low-clutter backdrop. The dummy itself is the visual anchor; its canvas/leather look should read as a classic practice target. On each confirmed hit, the impact VFX burst uses a warm accent color (orange/white spark or dust) at the exact contact point, paired with a sharp tactile 'thwack' SFX and a brief dummy flash/nudge (not a knockdown) to sell weight without breaking its stationary, indestructible read. The Hit Counter HUD sits top-center or top-right, bold and legible, with a subtle scale-punch pop animation on every increment to reinforce the 'practice and improve' reward loop; a visible reset control (key hint or button) sits near it. Overall tone is satisfying and snappy ('juice' over realism) — no gore, no heavy narrative, wide-audience training-room vibe.

requirements.description: Punches feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp warm-accent-colored impact VFX, and a sharp tactile impact SFX that together sell weight on every successful hit, matching a minimalist martial-arts training tone.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A minimalist martial-arts training theme: the fighter is a lone practitioner honing technique on a classic canvas/leather training dummy, evoking dojo practice rather than narrative combat. Tone is clean, focused, and satisfying — punches should feel punchy and rewarding through snappy animation timing, a crisp impact VFX (small spark/dust burst in a warm accent color like orange or white), and a sharp, tactile SFX (a solid 'thwack' or glove-impact sound) that together sell weight and feedback on every successful hit. The Hit Counter UI reinforces a 'practice and improve' motif — bold, legible numerals that pop with a subtle scale-punch animation each time they increment, turning repetition into a small, satisfying reward loop. No horror, gore, or heavy narrative elements; the aesthetic leans toward approachable, arcade-y training-room vibes suitable for a wide audience.
Tone is lighthearted/arcade training-room, not gritty or violent combat storytelling.
Visual and audio feedback prioritizes clarity and satisfaction ('juice') over realism.
No specific IP, character design, or story context was provided, so a generic 'lone fighter in training' framing is used as a safe default.
Color/style direction (e.g., warm accent VFX color) is a suggested default and can be swapped without affecting core mechanics.
requirements.acceptance: The combined VFX color/timing and SFX character read as a clean, satisfying 'thwack' consistent with a training-room tone rather than gritty combat, verified by inspecting the imported VFX/SFX assets.

A compact, single-room training environment — a simple gym or dojo-style space with a flat, evenly lit floor to keep focus on the player and dummy interaction. Layout: the target dummy is fixed at a central point in the room; the player spawns a few paces in front of it with open space around for repositioning and repeated approach-punch cycles. The Hit Counter UI is anchored to a consistent HUD position (commonly top-center or top-right of the screen) so it remains visible during gameplay without obstructing the action. Lighting is neutral and even (no dramatic shadows) to ensure the punch VFX and dummy reactions are clearly visible. The camera follows the player in third-person, framed to keep both the character and dummy in view during the punching interaction. No additional props, obstacles, or secondary areas are needed for this focused training-loop prototype; the space is intentionally small and uncluttered.
